primer.title: Artificial intelligence
primer.body: AI is software that can recognise patterns, work with language, make predictions and help with decisions. It is useful, but it can still make mistakes.

primer.title: Automation
primer.body: Automation is when a task or process happens with less manual effort. It follows rules and instructions so the same work does not have to be repeated by a person every time.

primer.title: When they work together
primer.body: AI can handle tasks that need interpretation; automation can move the result to the next step. Together, they can help a business respond, organise information or complete routine work.

lesson.title: Where AI meets automation
lesson.body_md: Imagine a small shop receiving orders online. Automation can record each order and send a confirmation. AI can help interpret a customer's question or sort an unclear message. The two can work together, while a person remains responsible for important decisions.
lesson.story_md: A customer sends a message asking whether a particular size is available. An AI tool can interpret the question. An automated workflow can check the stock system and send the result back, even when the shop is closed.
lesson.story_lesson: AI helps interpret the request. Automation connects the steps. The useful result comes from designing the whole process well.
lesson.check_prompt: What is the main difference between AI and automation?

check_options.A: They are two names for the same thing
check_options.B: AI can interpret or generate; automation carries out a defined process
check_options.C: Automation always needs AI to work

lesson.check_explanation: AI can interpret or generate information. Automation carries out a process, often using rules and connected tools.
